summaries: When the vault hook puts back a grant that a shell command outside the packaged autopilot.py created or widened, it now also puts back the arming record that the same command consumed. The runtime state then returns exactly to what the command found, and a sanctioned `on` can still complete the user's typed entry within the arming lifetime.

CI sets up one exact Python release on every shard of a run: the plan job records the release it resolved for the policy's major.minor, and every later job and shard sets up that release, so a toolcache update during a run no longer fails the check with a runtime that changed between shards.

New `context_pack.py` and `step_timing.py`, used only at the non-default values of process switches `context_pack` (`role_digest`) and `step_timing` (`recorded`, with budgets from `step_budgets`), so every default output and bound instruction is unchanged. `context_pack.py build` derives, per entry, role and mode, a deterministic digest of the rule units of the task's required reads (obligations, refusals, switch instructions and package commands), with every source and conditional read bound by sha256; a rule that names only another role of the entry is listed by id, and `check` refuses a pack whose sources changed or that a fresh build would not reproduce. `step_timing.py` records each flow step and role spawn (reading, writing, review, re-review, waiting) in a durable run file under `.agentrof/agent-marketplace/timing/`, reports a span that ends over its budget at once with its phase breakdown, largest contributor and lever, lists open spans already past budget, and writes a per-step report against the budgets. In one measured project, a one-story planning revision spent most of its writer time reading the full flow and rule set, and 31 of 68 minutes went to readers re-reading unchanged notes.

Delivery `init` cuts a slug derived from the goal at 48 characters and then drops a trailing hyphen, so a goal whose cut falls right after a word break no longer fails with `invalid Delivery slug`. An explicit `--slug` is validated as before.

`scripts/impact_closure.py` computes a change's impact closure over every relation form the vault keeps, read in tiers (generated relation views, typed front matter, relation blocks and body wikilinks, maps and navigation, then a targeted identifier search for gaps), with the tier recorded per edge. It proves unchanged approved notes by each owning compiler's approval hash, widens on a shared contract or the process policy, and reports graph gaps and tier disagreements, each with its evidence and a suggested fix the flow's writer applies through the owning compiler; both scripts are read-only and never write the vault (#441). `scripts/vault_query.py` answers closure, related, who-cites, path, find, hash, changed-since, gaps and text search from a disposable JSON index under the project runtime scratch, rebuilt incrementally by file hash. Nothing calls either tool until a process switch selects it.

Three process switches let an Item's fixed cost scale with its size, all off by default, so every default output and every bound instruction is unchanged (#432). Process switch `item_qa_tier` (`full_per_item` | `change_tier_per_item`): at `change_tier_per_item`, where the Verification Contract declares a change-level and an integration tier, an Item's QA gate runs the change-level tier and the Delivery runs the integration tier once before its pull request. Process switch `item_review_scale` (`fixed` | `by_change_size`): at `by_change_size`, the official code reviewer reads alone an Item whose frozen change is within the owner's limits on the measures `code-review/data/change-size-measures.json` declares. Process switch `item_cost_report` (`off` | `per_step`): at `per_step`, the Delivery Review carries each Item's fixed cost step by step, a missing timestamp reported as missing, never estimated.

Two process switches for parallel lanes, both off by default. Process switch `lane_table` (`off` | `recorded`): at `recorded`, the new `scripts/lane_table.py` records each lane's start and finish under the project-local runtime directory, lists the lanes a restarted session still has to launch, resume or retry, and refuses to start a lane already finished. Process switch `lane_isolation` (`shared_checkout` | `scratch_clone`): at `scratch_clone`, each parallel fix lane works in its own scratch clone, `lane_table.py start` refuses a lane working directory inside the main checkout, and `lane_table.py check` refuses when the main checkout's branch changed since the run began.

Process switch `level_change_map` (`off` | `assertion_map`), off by default, so every default output and every bound instruction is unchanged. At `assertion_map`, a scenario is converted by an Item when it is automation-required, the file of its automation target is one the Item changes, and its Test Plan `level` differs from the newest revision an integrated Item of its story recorded. The writer records, in the Item's verification runtime, each converted scenario's Then and the assertion lines that prove it at the integration base and in the candidate, each with a kind from `deliver/data/assertion-kinds.json` and its expected value; `delivery_verification.py assertion-map` prints the converted scenarios, the check and a template. The candidate binds the map, and `freeze` refuses a converted scenario without an entry, an entry for another scenario, a Then other than the Test Plan's, a side without an assertion and an assertion line its file does not hold. A pair whose after assertions only count or check existence while a before one compared a value, or that drops an expected value, is flagged in every reader's manifest for the code reviewer. In one measured project, an audit after four lanes moved three stories' live suites to unit tests found 35 weakened or vacuous expectations, and restoring them took 65 minutes.

Relicense from MIT to the Apache License 2.0 for future versions, with a NOTICE file and a trademark policy (TRADEMARKS.md). Plugin and marketplace manifests now declare `Apache-2.0`. Releases published before this change remain available under the MIT License.

Process switch `backlog_path` (`standard` | `light_when_eligible`), off by default so every default output is unchanged (#441). At `light_when_eligible`, a backlog revision of a technical or defect Requirement that changes at most a few technical or defect stories in one epic is reviewed by one reader of its story delta, and `backlog_compile.py record-light-root-review` writes the root review round from the compiler's structural checks; `light-path-status` reports eligibility and approval refuses a light root review the revision has outgrown. `backlog_compile.py stub-story --from-requirement` writes the story and test plan from the approved Requirement's acceptance items, work kind and evidence links.

A Verification Contract approval now stamps `paired_environment_revision` and `paired_environment_source_hash` from the approved current Environment Contract, and `operation_compile.py check --kind verification` reports a later Environment Contract approval as advisory drift under `paired_environment`. Writers no longer author the paired receipt, so a wrong draft hash cannot be written and the two contract writers can work side by side. In one measured project the receipt was re-authored in each of six review rounds, always after the other writer had finished.

Make bounded project context resolution the default task handoff, preserve manual discovery, exact revision receipts, nested conditions and full review fallback without approval history. Confine caches to the selected project and offer anonymous context feedback through an exact-payload user-approved issue protocol.

Process switch `requirement_fact_check` (`off` | `pre_approval_reader`), off by default (#422): at `pre_approval_reader`, before the approval question of a Requirement whose outcomes name contracts, scripts, files or test ids, one read-only low-tier reader checks those sentences against the files they cite and returns contradictions only, which the coordinator fixes before the owner sees the draft. In one measured project, Backlog Planning found four factual errors in one approved technical Requirement, which then took a second owner approval.

Requirement incorporation reads the approved root backlog review with the highest round number, so a round from 10 on no longer loses to round 9. A Requirement-mode root review carries a `Requirement Coverage` table with `requirement`, `story_ids` and `disposition`: `init`, `begin-revision` and `stub-backlog-review` write it and carry the previous round's rows, and once a story implements the backlog's Requirement, `check --pre-approval` and `approve` require exactly one row for it whose `story_ids` are exactly those stories. Manual mode is unchanged.

Process switches `review_scope` (`full` | `impact_closure`), `review_fanout` (`single_reader` | `per_unit`), `review_levels` (`sequential` | `concurrent_when_independent`), `context_pack` (`off` | `role_digest`), `step_timing` (`off` | `recorded`) and `step_budgets` (`off` | `enforced`), each off by default so every default output is unchanged (#441). Every flow anchors them at its reading and review steps: impact-closure reading with compiler structural checks before any reader, recorded beyond-closure reads, relation gaps reported for the writer to fix and delta-only confirmation re-reviews; one reader per changed unit plus one aggregator; independent review levels side by side; the role digest; step timing; and step budgets as reporting-only maximums with the initial targets as package limits. The constitution, every role prompt and every flow now navigate the task's bound inputs vault first: a role with a shell runs the query tools before tiered relation sources, a read-only reader follows its bound inputs' relations and the views its manifest binds, and only under review_scope impact_closure is a read beyond the given scope allowed and recorded; both host contracts carry the spawning rules.

Process switch `review_rounds` (`current` | `single_pass`), at its default today's behaviour: at `single_pass`, a backlog, Solution Design, Design System or Operation contract review runs one reader, never a lens panel, with no calibration reader; only a critical finding starts a writer pass and one re-review of the changed text, and minor and major findings become follow-ups, as the new switch reference `challenge-review/references/switch-review_rounds-single_pass.md` defines. `backlog_compile.py` and `operation_compile.py` then require no `Severity Calibration` row and accept a major finding in `Accepted Minor Findings`. In one measured project each contract revision ran a writer, two lens readers and a calibration reader per round, and the review loop took hours per contract.

At `review_scope: impact_closure` every reviewer input derivation reads the change's impact closure: `task_inputs.py` (business analysis, solution design, design system, experience, Operation contracts, delivery and execution planning, the execution-plan bundle readers), `backlog_review_inputs.py` (epic and root readers) and `delivery_verification.py manifest` (code review and QA). A note the closure proves unchanged is listed with its approval hash and current sha256 instead of being read, every role starts from the vault's relation views, a reader carries a `beyond_closure` list for any read past the closure, and a confirmation re-check given findings and the reviewed commit reads only the fixed lines' notes and what the fix touches. At `context_pack: role_digest` a task binds the role digest and its `pack_hash` instead of its required reads and checks the pack before a result is kept. At the defaults every task, manifest and verification manifest is derived as released.

A task given explicit inputs, outside an exact epic and a code review base, now binds those inputs and the notes they cite by content, the rest of the canonical source inventory by path only under `canonical_source_paths`, and leaves `head` out of its `source_hash`. A new or removed source still makes the task stale, while a commit or a write to an unrelated note leaves it fresh, so independent writers and review panels no longer stale each other. In one measured project about a dozen parallel writer passes each hit a stale manifest and one review panel was restarted.

Process switch `test_levels` (`off` | `declared`), off by default, so every default output and every bound instruction is unchanged. A Test Plan scenario may state `level`, `unit`, `fixture` or `live`, and a `level_reason`, what has to be real for its assertion to mean something; `backlog_compile.py check` refuses a `level` outside the three values whenever a scenario states it, at every value. At `declared`, QA proves a decision rule at `unit` level over every combination of its inputs, adds one `fixture` scenario per entry point and decision family and keeps `live` for engine or operating-system behaviour, and `backlog_compile.py check --json` and the epic and root review manifests list under `test_levels` each automation-required scenario that states no level and each `fixture` or `live` one that states no reason. The `test_cost_budget` serial-rows list then names each flagged scenario's level, and the backlog reviewer asks of every `live` scenario whether its assertion is a decision. The list is advisory and never fails a check or blocks a review. In one measured project, a final gate ran 166 live cases in 227 minutes, about 82 seconds per case, and a later story's Test Plan asked for 41 scenarios, most of them live, although about 40 in-process unit tests that ran in about a second already proved the decision rules behind most of them.

Tests follow a unit-first rule (#446): a rule a unit test can prove is tested in process on synthetic input, each script or verb keeps one real end-to-end smoke, and integration tests remain only for races, multi-Delivery interplay and real Git semantics. The Delivery Git, verification, task-input, Experience record revision and setup scripts expose their decisions as pure functions their existing paths call, with unchanged order and messages, so the converted tests call them directly. The two open #377 items split the cancellation test into its three scenarios and move the control and receipt tampering cases of the architecture push test to unit cases, with a per-process stamped Item seed for the cases only Git can show. Context resolver coverage from main is classified at the same boundary; approval events, light scope decisions and timing rules run locally in process. Unit workers reject fixture process starts, drain threads under the guard and isolate mutable validator fixtures.
